description: Curated paraphrased evidence notes based on linked scholarly papers. These are not verbatim abstracts and are intended for claim-suggestion RAG, not citation identity verification.

records.title: Attention Is All You Need
records.summary: Introduces the Transformer, an encoder-decoder architecture based on attention rather than recurrence or convolution. Self-attention relates tokens within a sequence and enables substantially more parallel computation during training than recurrent sequence processing.

records.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
records.summary: Introduces BERT, which pretrains deep bidirectional representations by conditioning on left and right context. The pretrained model can be fine-tuned for tasks such as question answering and language inference with a small task-specific output layer.

records.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
records.summary: Studies how training data size, optimization choices, and hyperparameters affect BERT-style pretraining. The authors report that BERT was undertrained under its original setup and show that careful optimization can improve downstream benchmark results.

records.title: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientific Text
records.summary: Introduces SciBERT, pretrained on a large multi-domain corpus of scientific publications. Evaluation covers sequence tagging, sentence classification, and dependency parsing; the paper reports statistically significant improvements over BERT on several scientific NLP tasks, not a universal fixed percentage gain.

records.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
records.summary: Combines a pretrained sequence-to-sequence generator with a dense retriever over an external document collection. The study evaluates knowledge-intensive NLP tasks and reports gains on selected benchmarks. Retrieval provides explicit supporting documents, but this does not establish that RAG eliminates hallucinations or reduces errors by a fixed percentage in every application.

records.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
records.summary: Evaluates GPT-3, a 175-billion-parameter autoregressive language model, in zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot settings. Scaling improves performance on many studied tasks, while results vary by task and do not imply that large models are always correct.

records.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
records.summary: Presents T5, which casts a broad range of NLP tasks into a text-to-text format and studies transfer-learning choices including objectives, datasets, and scale. Its results show strong performance on evaluated benchmarks rather than universal superiority on all possible tasks.

records.title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding
records.summary: Introduces XLNet, using permutation language modeling to capture bidirectional context while retaining an autoregressive objective. The paper evaluates the approach on language-understanding benchmarks and compares it with prior pretrained models.

records.title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators
records.summary: Proposes replaced-token detection: a model learns to identify tokens replaced by a small generator rather than predicting only masked tokens. The authors report improved compute efficiency and strong downstream results under their tested training settings.

records.title: DeBERTa: Decoding-enhanced BERT with Disentangled Attention
records.summary: Introduces disentangled attention that represents content and position separately, together with an enhanced mask decoder. The paper reports improvements over comparison systems on several natural-language understanding and generation benchmarks.

records.title: An Image Is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
records.summary: Applies a pure Transformer directly to sequences of image patches. With large-scale pretraining and transfer to image-recognition benchmarks, the Vision Transformer matches or outperforms leading convolutional networks in the studied settings.

records.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
records.summary: Presents residual learning, where layers learn residual functions relative to their inputs, enabling the training of substantially deeper networks. The paper demonstrates results on image-recognition benchmarks; it does not imply deeper models always perform better in every setting.

records.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
records.summary: Trains a deep convolutional neural network on the ImageNet classification task. The reported model achieved substantially lower top-1 and top-5 error than the previous state of the art in that benchmark and helped establish deep CNNs for large-scale image recognition.

records.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
records.summary: Introduces Adam, an optimizer using adaptive estimates of first and second moments of gradients. The paper reports favorable empirical results on evaluated problems, but does not establish that Adam achieves lower validation loss than SGD for every model, dataset, or learning-rate schedule.

records.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
records.summary: Introduces efficient architectures for learning continuous word vectors from large text collections. The paper evaluates vector quality on word-similarity and related tasks and reports useful semantic and syntactic representations with lower training cost.

records.title: Long Short-Term Memory
records.summary: Introduces LSTM memory cells and constant-error-flow mechanisms designed to address decaying error signals and learn long time lags in recurrent networks. This supports the claim that LSTM was designed to mitigate the problem, not the stronger claim that it eliminates all vanishing gradients or always learns arbitrary-length dependencies.

records.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
records.summary: Introduces a framework with a generator and discriminator trained through an adversarial minimax objective. The discriminator helps distinguish generated from real samples during training; discriminator accuracy alone is not a guarantee that generated samples are realistic or that training has converged well.

records.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
records.summary: Presents an end-to-end sequence-to-sequence approach with one multilayer LSTM encoding an input sequence and another decoding the output. Experiments on English-to-French translation show competitive results and the model handles the long sentences tested.

records.title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
records.summary: Introduces ELMo contextual word representations derived from internal states of a deep bidirectional language model. The representations can be added to task-specific models and show gains on several evaluated language-understanding tasks.

records.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
records.summary: Adds a differentiable attention mechanism that lets a translation decoder focus on relevant parts of a source sentence rather than relying on one fixed-length vector. The authors report competitive English-to-French translation results and interpretable soft alignments.

records.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
records.summary: Adapts BERT with siamese and triplet network structures to produce sentence embeddings that can be compared with cosine similarity. This makes large-scale semantic similarity search much more efficient than separately processing every sentence pair with BERT.

records.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
records.summary: Studies a dense dual-encoder retriever for open-domain question answering. On the datasets evaluated, the method improves top-20 passage retrieval accuracy over a strong BM25 baseline; those results are empirical findings on selected benchmarks, not a guarantee of superiority for every corpus or query type.

records.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
records.summary: Introduces a heterogeneous benchmark spanning 18 retrieval datasets and several retrieval model families. Results show that retrieval performance and generalization vary across settings; BM25 is a strong baseline, while neural ranking approaches can improve quality with trade-offs in computational cost.

records.title: Retrieval Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
records.summary: Augments language-model pretraining with a learned retriever that accesses an external document corpus. The study evaluates open-domain question answering and reports improvements on the studied benchmarks, illustrating how retrieved knowledge can complement parametric model knowledge.

records.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
records.summary: Studies a sequence-to-sequence generator that reads multiple retrieved passages for open-domain question answering. Results on Natural Questions and TriviaQA improve when more passages are retrieved in the tested setting, suggesting that generators can aggregate complementary evidence. More retrieved passages do not guarantee correctness in every setting.

records.title: Matryoshka Representation Learning
records.summary: Proposes representations trained to retain useful information at multiple embedding dimensions. The work studies accuracy-efficiency trade-offs and reports that smaller truncated embeddings can retain strong performance for selected tasks. It does not support a universal rule that increasing embedding dimension always improves retrieval accuracy.
